title: Fix four bugs and dead code in a Rust statistics library
description: A Rust stats library has four bugs: mean() crashes on empty input, median() is wrong for even-length slices, normalize() panics when all values are equal, and mode() has a dead unused variable. Fix all four.

task_spec.prompt:
The Rust library in src/lib.rs has four problems:

1. mean() divides by values.len() even when the slice is empty, producing NaN or a panic. Change its signature to fn mean(values: &[f64]) -> Option<f64> — return None for empty, Some(mean) otherwise. Update the existing test to unwrap the Option.

2. median() returns sorted[mid] which for even-length slices gives the upper-middle element instead of the average of the two middle elements. Fix it to return the average of sorted[mid-1] and sorted[mid] for even-length. Update test_median_even to assert the correct value (2.5 for [1,2,3,4]).

3. normalize() panics when min==max (all values identical) because it divides by zero. Fix it: when max==min, return a vec of all 0.0s instead of panicking. Add a test test_normalize_uniform that passes &[5.0, 5.0, 5.0] and asserts the result is all 0.0.

4. mode() has a dead `let unused = 42;` variable. Remove it. Also remove the now-unused `use std::collections::HashMap` if mode is the only user — but keep HashMap if still needed.

All cargo tests must pass after your changes. cargo clippy -- -D warnings must be clean (no dead_code warnings).
required_artifacts: median() correct for even-length slices (returns average of two middles)
normalize() returns all-zeros for uniform input instead of panicking
success_criteria: All four bugs fixed with appropriate type changes
followup_prompts: Run `cargo test` to check the current state. Walk me through what bugs you found and fixed. If any tests are still failing, show me the errors and fix them.
Final verification: run `cargo test` and confirm a completely clean build. Every test must pass — if any are still red, fix them now.
